answer: Before an agent may vote or mine, it must lock a bonded jade reserve at a public inlet whose receipt is hashed onto the ledger and rechecked by a live sparrow probe that confirms the stake is still unspent and time-stamped to this identity. Peers verify that hash against the bond contract; a second persona requires posting a fresh equal lock that slashes if clustering is later proven, so each fake identity costs at least one full stake linearly, and worse when correlated slashing multiplies the loss.
